title: Dual Automatic Temperature Control: Understanding the Controls
introduction: I read automatic climate control like a household thermostat with separate seats to please: choose the cabin temperature you want, and the system manages heating or cooling toward it. The useful distinction is between the temperature target and the amount of air moving. This overview explains those controls on vehicles with DATC, including independent side settings and moisture reduction during A/C operation. It is a controls guide, not a performance test.

edits.text: The Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC) system maintains the selected interior temperature by heating and/or cooling the air according to selections made on the HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) control panel.
edits.why: The selected temperature is the goal the system works toward. Keeping that goal separate from airflow makes the controls easier to understand.

edits.text: The driver can override automatic operation.
edits.why: Automatic control does not remove the driver’s ability to intervene; an override changes how the system is being commanded.

edits.text: Use the temperature setting to select the cabin air temperature you want.
edits.why: I read this as the desired cabin condition, rather than as a measurement of the air currently leaving a vent.

edits.text: Use the blower motor control override buttons to vary blower motor speed.
edits.why: The blower moves cabin air. Its speed changes airflow, which is a different job from selecting the temperature target.

edits.text: Set the driver-side and passenger-side temperatures individually when different settings are wanted.
edits.why: Separate temperature requests are a normal capability of this system, so different selected settings on the two sides are not themselves evidence of a fault.

edits.text: During A/C operation, the system also reduces the relative humidity of the air inside the vehicle.
edits.why: Cooling has a moisture-management benefit as well as a temperature effect. That helps explain why A/C operation concerns more than simply making the cabin colder.
